literal_source_claim_en: An upper-bound estimate for a determinant.
source_attribution: Jacques Hadamard, 1893 (catalog metadata; exact source proposition not yet admitted)
statement_blocker: The catalog gives only a determinant-upper-bound gloss. It does not fix real versus complex scalars, finite index and dimension, rows versus columns, Euclidean norm and determinant encodings, squared versus unsquared form, equality scope, ordered binders, or degenerate cases. The pinned real volume-form theorem and determinant bridges are strong candidates, but selecting their composition as canonical at intake would silently add clauses and substitute a coordinate-free formulation before source admission and checked transport.
domain_and_universes: Open: an admitted source must choose real or complex finite square matrices, an explicit Fin n or arbitrary finite index, or a coordinate-free real n-dimensional inner product space; all universes and instance binders remain open.
conclusion: Open: likely the absolute determinant is at most the product of Euclidean row or column norms; the catalog does not specify the formula or whether equality conditions are included.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before root selection; dimension zero and one, zero or singular matrices, zero rows or columns, diagonal and orthogonal-row matrices, proportional rows, empty products, determinant sign, and equality cases all require source-mapped decisions.
